{{Short description|Polyhedron with 60 faces}}
{{Uniform polyhedra db|Uniform dual polyhedron stat table|rI}}
In [[geometry]], the '''rhombicosacron''' (or '''midly dipteral ditriacontahedron''') is a nonconvex [[Isohedral figure|isohedral]] [[polyhedron]]. It is the [[Dual polyhedron|dual]] of the [[nonconvex uniform polyhedron|uniform]] [[rhombicosahedron]], U56. It has 50 [[Vertex (geometry)|vertices]], 120 [[Edge (geometry)|edges]], and 60 [[crossed-quadrilateral]] faces.

== Proportions==
Each face has two angles of <math>\arccos(\frac{3}{4})\approx 41.409\,622\,109\,27^{\circ}</math> and two angles of <math>\arccos(-\frac{1}{6})\approx 99.594\,068\,226\,86^{\circ}</math>. The diagonals of each antiparallelogram  intersect at an angle of <math>\arccos(\frac{1}{8}+\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{24})\approx 38.996\,309\,663\,87^{\circ}</math>. The [[dihedral angle]] equals <math>\arccos(-\frac{5}{7})\approx 135.584\,691\,402\,81^{\circ}</math>. The ratio between the lengths of the long edges and the short ones equals <math>\frac{3}{2}+\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{5}</math>, which is the square of the [[golden ratio]].
